item.title: Lyndon McLeod Named Future Victims In His Novels
item.description: Lyndon McLeod killed five people in Denver and Lakewood in December 2021. His novels, which named two victims in fictional killings, became part of the investigation. The attacks ended when a wounded police officer shot and killed him.

item.title: Over 20 Missed Chances To Stop Beastie House Abuse
item.description: Three children were abused in Glasgow’s “Beastie House” between 2012 and 2019. Seven offenders received prison sentences with lifelong restrictions in 2025. A 2026 review identified more than 20 missed opportunities for agencies to intervene and protect the children.

item.title: She Tried To Kill Him. Then She Cross-Examined Him
item.description: Sheila Davalloo’s husband survived her 2003 attack. Nine years later, she represented herself and questioned him at her trial for murdering romantic rival Anna Lisa Raymundo. Her convictions brought consecutive prison sentences totaling 75 years.

item.title: He Taunted The CCTV Camera That Caught His Murder
item.description: Stephen Griffiths gestured at a CCTV camera after killing Suzanne Blamires in Bradford. A caretaker reviewing the footage alerted police. In December 2010, the criminology student pleaded guilty to murdering three women and received whole-life sentences.

item.title: Her Stalker Paid $250 To Find Her Front Door
item.description: Robert Bardo paid a private investigator to find actress Rebecca Schaeffer’s address through DMV records. He killed the 21-year-old at her Los Angeles home in 1989. Convicted of first-degree murder in 1991, he received life without parole.

item.title: She Killed The Friends Who Helped Her Fit In
item.description: Christine Paolilla was 17 when she participated in four killings in Clear Lake, Texas, including those of two friends who had helped her fit in at school. An anonymous tip broke the case three years later. In 2008, she was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to life.
